_comment: The standalone sign-off engines this fork adds, and whether the composed EDA image
They were repo-root Python that NO shipped artefact contained: tools/klayout/Dockerfile's
publish stage is `FROM scratch` + `COPY --from=build /klayout/bld`, and /klayout/bld is
build.sh's OUTPUT directory -- build.sh never installs repo-root Python, so all twelve
entry points were absent from the released image and $VIBEIC_KLAYOUT_TOOLS was unset in it.
The C++ ports of some of these ops inside dbSVRFEngine DO ship, via the `svrfdrc` buddy;
what did not ship is the standalone Python.
`install_dir` is what the image stages under $VIBEIC_KLAYOUT_TOOLS. The plugin's
`_klayout_launch.find_engine` accepts both this hyphenated spelling and its own underscored
one, so no directory is renamed to make the override resolve.
run_shipped_engines_test.sh asserts every declared directory and entry point exists, and --
the half that matters -- that no NEW engine directory appears in the tree undeclared. An
engine added next to its feature and shipped by nothing is the exact defect this file
closes, so silence is not an option: a new directory must be declared ship=true or ship=false
